---
title: "Omarchy autologin and requiring a password after boot"
status: wip
---

Omarchy is designed around full-disk encryption plus automatic login after the disk has been unlocked. If that security model is not what you want, SDDM autologin can be disabled so the account password is required as well.

Last checked against Omarchy 4.0.1 on 2026-09-05.

## first, find the active SDDM autologin file

The filename has changed across Omarchy versions, so do not assume it is always called `autologin.conf`.

```bash
sudo grep -R -n '^\[Autologin\]' /etc/sddm.conf /etc/sddm.conf.d 2>/dev/null
```

Recent Omarchy installs have used paths such as:

```text
/etc/sddm.conf.d/autologin.conf
/etc/sddm.conf.d/00-autologin.conf
```

## disable autologin

Back up the file returned by the command above, then remove or disable its `[Autologin]` configuration.

For example, if the file is `/etc/sddm.conf.d/00-autologin.conf`:

```bash
sudo cp /etc/sddm.conf.d/00-autologin.conf /etc/sddm.conf.d/00-autologin.conf.bak
sudoedit /etc/sddm.conf.d/00-autologin.conf
```

Remove or comment the `[Autologin]` section, then restart SDDM:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart sddm
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Restarting SDDM immediately ends the graphical session. Save your work first.
:::

## caveats

Omarchy is still primarily a single-user system. Its current SDDM theme is intentionally minimal and is not a full desktop/session chooser.

There have also been open Omarchy 4.0.1 reports involving SDDM login behavior. Keep a TTY available while testing (`Ctrl+Alt+F2` or another function key) so you can restore the backup if the graphical login does not work.
